description: Rank markets by how far their funding has diverged from a benchmark (default ETH) over a trailing window. Pick bar (1d, the default, or 1h for completed hours) to read completed days or completed hours. day defaults to the last complete interval. metric=rate compares mean funding over the window; metric=cum_funding_spread compares how far a market's cumulative funding level travelled inside the window (its high minus its low, so never negative) — that is not the funding the window accumulated: for that, read funding_paid from query_series and sum it. Returns the most diverged in each direction, each row with usd_volume_avg so a spread can be sized; pass min_usd_volume_7d_avg (USD/day) to exclude markets too illiquid to trade the divergence in. Markets with no funding reading are excluded from both lists. Descriptive only.

bar.description:
`1d` (the default) for completed UTC days, `1h` for completed UTC hours.
An interval, at either grain, is stamped by the instant it **closes** —
an hourly `…T09:00:00Z` is the hour that ended at 09:00.

benchmark.description: The market whose funding is the yardstick. Defaults to ETH.

day.description:
The day or hour to rank as of: `YYYY-MM-DD` or `latest` at `bar: 1d`, a
completed `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:00:00Z` (the hour that *ended* there) or `latest`
at `bar: 1h`.

metric.description:
`rate` (the default) ranks each market's mean funding over the window
minus the benchmark's; `cum_funding_spread` ranks the **spread of the
cumulative funding level** over the window — its high minus its low, so
always non-negative — minus the benchmark's. That is not the funding the
window accumulated: `cum_funding` is a running total, so a market whose
level retraced has a large spread and a *negative* accumulation (and one
that reversed inside the window has a spread several times its true
accumulation). Measured 2026-10-13 over 34 markets and the trailing 168
hours, the expression below reproduced the served value exactly, while
`SUM(funding_paid)` over the same window disagreed in sign for 11 of
them (TRX +0.00440 vs −0.00445) and by up to 100× (CASHCAT 0.2050 vs
0.0020). The accumulation is not a served field; read `funding_paid`
from `query_series` and sum it over the window you want instead.

min_usd_volume_7d_avg.description:
Drop markets whose average **daily** traded notional over the divergence
window is below this value, in USD/day at either bar. Each row carries
that figure as `usd_volume_avg`, so the floor decides which spreads are
tradeable rather than which are largest.

top_n.description:
Markets per ranked list, 1..100 (values outside are clamped to the
nearest bound and the response says so). Defaults to 10.

window_days.description: Length of the trailing window in days, 1..365. Defaults to 7.

name: funding_divergence

DivergenceRow.description: One market's funding divergence from the benchmark.

usd_volume_avg.description:
Mean traded notional per interval over the same window, in USD/day at
either grain. A funding spread is only as interesting as the size a
position in it can take, and the widest divergence in a slice is
regularly a quiet day in an illiquid market — read this column before
reading `divergence`.

value.description: This market's value for the requested metric over the window.

bar.description: The grain this answer was computed at: `1d` or `1h`.

benchmark_value.description: The benchmark's own value for the metric.

eligible_count.description: Markets left after your explicit market filter.

matched_count.description:
Markets that had a funding reading in the window. Markets without one are
excluded from both lists and from this count — a missing reading must
never appear as an extreme.

top_negative.description:
The largest divergences toward the benchmark's opposite, most extreme
first.

top_positive.description: The largest divergences away from the benchmark, most extreme first.

visible_count.description:
Markets in your plan's slice on this interval, before any filter you
passed.

title: Funding divergence
